name: Basin Lake
note: Lake: a black-water perched dune lake on K'gari, about a football oval in area and 8 m deep, a stop beside Lake McKenzie.

name: Bogimbah Creek
note: Creek: the largest creek on K'gari, 8 km north of Kingfisher Bay, named as a water feature on the island's formation page; a walk or stop rather than a destination.

name: The Pinnacles
note: Coloured sand cliffs: 72 colours of sand north of Eli Creek on K'gari's east coast, also called the Coloured Sands; visited on foot and by 4WD.

name: Stonetool Sand Blow
note: Sand blow: an active mobile dune on K'gari uncovering an ancient buried forest, named for stone tools found there.

name: 75 Mile Beach
note: Beach highway: the 75 Mile Beach on K'gari's east coast, driven at 80 km/h, with birds of prey, sea birds and dingoes; the island's main road.

name: Royal Rainforest
note: Rainforest: the subtropical rainforest of K'gari's central gullies, with satinay trees, kauri pines and king ferns, visited on foot.

name: Rainbow Beach
note: Town: a coastal village and the mainland gateway to K'gari and Inskip Point, with coloured sand cliffs and sand blows near it.

name: Carlo Sand Blow
note: Sand blow: a short walk from Rainbow Beach, with postcard views, named as a paragliding and hang-gliding spot.

name: Coloured Sands Rainbow Beach
note: Coloured sand cliffs: a longer walk along the beach from Rainbow Beach, banded in reds and yellows. Check against the K'gari Pinnacles entry before placing; the two may be one feature.

name: Inskip Point
note: Headland: the point at the tip of the peninsula where the K'gari ferry leaves, with views over the island.

name: Wolf Rock
note: Dive site: a reef off Rainbow Beach where divers meet sharks; a dive, not a walk, so a visitor needs an operator.

name: Lady Elliot Island
note: Island: a coral cay at the southern end of the Great Barrier Reef with a resort, a lighthouse and snorkelling and diving sites; reached by air or boat from Bundaberg or Hervey Bay.

name: Lady Musgrave Island
note: Island: a coral cay in the Southern Great Barrier Reef reached by boat from Bundaberg, with an underwater observatory named by the Bundaberg site.

name: Mon Repos Beach
note: Beach: the beach at Mon Repos, named beside the turtle rookery; the rookery itself is the Mon Repos Conservation Park entry.

name: Turtle Sands
note: Beach: a named beach at Mon Repos on the Bundaberg coast, listed beside the turtle rookery.

name: Elliott Heads Rock Pools
note: Rock pools: tidal rock pools at Elliott Heads, named on the Bundaberg site.

name: Elliott Heads Beach
note: Beach: the beach at Elliott Heads, on the Bundaberg coast, named on the Bundaberg site.

name: Dr Mays Island
note: Island: a small island off Elliott Heads named as a Bundaberg-coast stop; access and visitor facilities unconfirmed.

name: South Head Parklands
note: Parkland: the South Head parklands and playground at Burnett Heads, named on the Bundaberg site.

name: Oaks Beach
note: Beach: a beach near Burnett Heads, named on the Bundaberg site; details unread.

name: Monsoon Aquatics Coral Farm
note: Coral farm tour: Australia's largest coral farm at Burnett Heads, with a one-hour behind-the-scenes tour of coral propagation; an operator venue.

name: Bundaberg Port Marina
note: Marina: the port marina at Burnett Heads, a base for reef and fishing boats rather than a stop in itself.

name: Noor'garr Walla Lookout
note: Lookout: the Whale Rock lookout at Bargara, named on the Bundaberg site.

name: Mary Kinross Park
note: Park: a park at Bargara on the Coral Coast, named on the Bundaberg site; details unread.

name: Bargara Headlands Yarning Circle
note: Cultural site: a yarning circle on the Bargara headlands, named on the Bundaberg site.

name: Moore Park Wetlands
note: Wetlands: a wetland beside Moore Park Beach, named on the Bundaberg site; details unread.

name: Childers Historical Street Walk
note: Heritage walk: a self-guided walk through the historic streets of Childers, past its heritage buildings.

name: Old Pharmacy Museum
note: Museum: the Old Pharmacy Museum in Childers, named on the Bundaberg site.

name: Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo
note: Wildlife park: a reptile park and zoo at Childers, named on the Bundaberg site.

name: Russo Nature Park
note: Nature park: a nature park near Childers, named on the Bundaberg site; details unread.

name: Childers Arts Space
note: Gallery: the Childers Arts Space, named on the Bundaberg site; details unread.

name: Promisedland Road Mountain Biking Trails
note: Mountain bike trails: a set of mountain bike trails on Promisedland Road near Childers, a riding stop.

name: Milpi Magic Mosaics Trail
note: Trail: the Milpi Magic Mosaics Trail, a drive-and-walk trail named on the Bundaberg site; location and details unread.

name: Bundaberg CBD Heritage Walk
note: Heritage walk: a walking route through Bundaberg's central heritage buildings and historic hotels.

name: Bourbong Street Heritage Walk
note: Heritage walk: the Bourbong Street civic heart of Bundaberg, with grand heritage buildings, historic hotels and shopfronts.

name: Cania Gorge National Park
note: National park: a sandstone gorge with eight walks, caves and dry rainforest, in the North Burnett and reached from Bundaberg.

name: Dragon Cave
note: Cave: a natural 'dragon'-shaped cave in Cania Gorge National Park, reached on a sandstone walk.

name: King Orchid Crevice
note: Crevice: a rock crevice on the Two Storey Cave circuit in Cania Gorge National Park.

name: The Overhang (Cania Gorge)
note: Overhang: a striking sandstone overhang in Cania Gorge National Park, a stop on the gorge walks.

name: HMAS Tobruk
note: Wreck dive: the former navy ship sunk as an artificial reef off the Fraser Coast, dived from Hervey Bay operators.

name: Tasman Venture
note: Dive vessel: a dive boat that runs reef and wreck trips from Hervey Bay; a vessel and operator, so likely not a spot itself.
